abstract: 'This post reports an experiment on the reproducibility of research conducted with generative artificial intelligence (AI). Forty-eight Claude Code agents running Claude Opus 5.5 received one analysis question about a semantic-priming data set simulated with pilotr, in a request that either left the analysis open or specified it. Half answered in prose without running code, and half wrote an R script that was then executed. No two texts were identical, but scripts given the same request and data printed the same result. Prose replies were as consistent as the scripts on balanced data, where the mixed model reduces to a few mean squares and cross-products, but took far longer when the request specified the analysis. On unbalanced data, they gave approximations, none of which matched the executed result. Every script printed identical output each time it was executed in its recorded environment, including a rebuild of it on another machine. Under newer versions of R and its packages, the scripts printed the same results, and restoring the recorded version of lme4 traced the only change, in formatting, to its update. The discussion draws on many-analysts studies and on research into nondeterminism in language models and into human interaction with automation. It argues that executed code supplies the exactness and the checkable record of an AI-assisted analysis, whereas the agreement between runs depended here on the model and the task. It also argues that researchers need to be able to specify, read and check the code that agents write.'

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# last commit that changed them, so that a reader sees the files this page was
# built from. While they have uncommitted changes, or outside a git repository,
# the links point to master.
last_commit <- function(path) tryCatch({
  changed <- system2('git', c('status', '--porcelain', '--', path), stdout = TRUE)
  commit <- system2('git', c('log', '-1', '--format=%H', '--', path), stdout = TRUE)
  if (length(changed) == 0 && length(commit) == 1) commit else 'master'
}, error = function(e) 'master', warning = function(w) 'master')
experiment_ref <- last_commit(experiment)
experiment_url <- function(path = '', type = 'blob') {
  sprintf('https://github.com/pablobernabeu/website-files/%s/%s/content/post/reproducible-research-with-generative-ai/experiment/%s',
          type, experiment_ref, path)
}

# Counts in the prose follow APA style: words for zero to nine, numerals from
# 10 and numerals for a count set beside one of 10 or more ('3 of 16').
count_text <- function(x, compared_with = NULL) {
  words <- c('zero', 'one', 'two', 'three', 'four', 'five', 'six', 'seven',
             'eight', 'nine')
  if (x == round(x) && x >= 0 && max(c(x, compared_with)) < 10) words[x + 1]
  else format(x, big.mark = ',', scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
}
# Negative numbers in the prose and tables take a true minus sign, written as an
# HTML entity so that it survives a build in any locale.
minus <- function(x) gsub('-', '&minus;', x, fixed = TRUE)
ms <- function(x, digits = 2) minus(formatC(x, format = 'f', digits = digits))
interval <- function(lower, upper, digits = 2) sprintf('[%s, %s]', ms(lower, digits), ms(upper, digits))
```

Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is now used at many stages of research, from reading the literature to writing and analysing. Each of its replies is a sample, drawn one token at a time from a probability distribution, so the same request can return a different reply (Holtzman et al., 2020). Reproducibility, in the sense set out by the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine (2019, p. 46), means obtaining consistent results from the same input data, computational steps, methods, code and conditions of analysis. A reply in a chat window meets few of those conditions, since its computations happen out of view and the settings that shaped it are rarely shown.

Agentic tools such as Claude Code can instead read a project, edit its files and run commands, on the researcher's own computer or in a cloud session (Anthropic, n.d.-b). OpenAI (2026) describes ChatGPT Work as acting across a user's apps and files to turn a goal into finished documents, spreadsheets and web apps. When such a tool writes an R or Python script, the model's variability enters while the script is written. Once saved, the script is as deterministic as any other code, and it can be read, tested, kept under version control and executed again.

This post examines that division of labour with an experiment. A Claude Code session put one analysis question, about a semantic-priming data set simulated with my [pilotr](/2026/pilotr-pilot-the-study-before-running-it/) package (Bernabeu, 2026b), to `r count_text(nrow(design))` Claude Code agents. Half of them answered in prose, as a chat assistant without a code interpreter would, and half wrote an R script that was then executed. The results bear on two questions: what executing code adds to an AI-assisted analysis and what the researcher needs to know of R to specify, read and check the code that an agent writes.

## Development

This section reviews the sources of variation in the output of language models and the case for moving computation into code, and then describes the data and the design of the experiment.

### Where the Variation Comes From

Setting the sampling temperature to zero, which should select the most probable token at every step, does not make hosted models deterministic. When Ouyang et al. (2025) asked ChatGPT at its default temperature to write code for 829 programming problems, repeated requests never returned code with the same test output for 47.56% to 75.76% of the problems, depending on the benchmark. A temperature of zero reduced that variation without removing it. Atıl et al. (2025) ran five hosted models 10 times on each of eight tasks with settings meant to be deterministic, and accuracy varied by up to 15 percentage points across runs. He and Thinking Machines Lab (2025) traced much of this behaviour to inference servers, where the number of requests processed together varies with load and changes the result of any kernel whose floating-point arithmetic depends on it. In their test with an open model, 1,000 completions of one prompt at temperature zero contained 80 distinct texts, and kernels made invariant to the batch size brought them down to one. Anthropic (n.d.-a) states that results will not be fully deterministic even at temperature zero, and its most recent models accept only the default temperature (Anthropic, n.d.-c).

Sampling is one source of variation among several. Chen et al. (2024) found substantial changes in behaviour between the March and June 2023 versions of the two models behind ChatGPT, one of which classified numbers as prime or composite with 84% accuracy in March and 51% in June. Meaning-preserving changes in the format of a prompt altered the accuracy of one open model by up to 76 percentage points in few-shot tasks (Sclar et al., 2024). When models annotated text for hypothesis tests, the choice of model and prompting strategy led to incorrect conclusions for about one in three hypotheses with state-of-the-art models (Baumann et al., 2025). Providers can also change closed models at any time (Spirling, 2023), which is one reason Palmer et al. (2024) argue that research using them needs explicit justification. In a chat interface, none of these sources is under the user's control, and few are recorded.

### Moving the Computation Into Code

Reproducible computational research asks that every result be traceable to the steps that produced it, without manual data manipulation. Scripts should be kept under version control, the versions of external programs archived and random seeds recorded (Sandve et al., 2013; see also Peng, 2011; Wilson et al., 2017). A script that an agent writes into a project under version control documents the steps behind a result, but the software environment has to be recorded as well. When Trisovic et al. (2022) re-executed R files deposited with published research data, allowing each a fixed time, 75% of those that finished within it stopped with an error, and 60% still did after automatic code cleaning. A lockfile from renv (Ushey & Wickham, 2026) and a record of the R session reduce that risk and show what has changed when a script behaves differently elsewhere.

### The Simulated Data

The data set used in the experiment was simulated with pilotr, which generates data in R and in Python from a portable design specification. Because pilotr draws its random numbers from its own generator, and the specification used here rounds the reaction times to whole milliseconds, the same specification and seed produce identical data in both languages (Bernabeu, 2026b). The specification describes `r spec_file$units$subject$n` participants who each respond to `r spec_file$units$item$n` words, once after a related prime and once after an unrelated one. Reaction times follow a shifted lognormal distribution, with a word-frequency covariate and with by-participant and by-item random intercepts and priming slopes.

```{r}
cat(readLines(file.path(experiment, 'spec.json')), sep = '\n')
```

The code below regenerates in R the file the agents analysed and compares its checksum with those of the original and of the same data generated by [the Python implementation](`r experiment_url('make_data.py')`).

```{r}
library(pilotr)

spec <- load_spec(file.path(experiment, 'spec.json'))
simulated <- simulate_design(spec)
regenerated <- data.frame(
  participant = sprintf('P%02d', simulated$subject),
  item = sprintf('W%02d', simulated$item),
  prime = simulated$prime,
  frequency = round(simulated$frequency, 2),
  rt = simulated$rt
)
# A binary connection keeps the line endings '\n' on every operating system.
regenerated_file <- tempfile(fileext = '.csv')
connection <- file(regenerated_file, 'wb')
write.csv(regenerated, connection, row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
close(connection)

checksums <- c(
  `regenerated in R` = digest::digest(file = regenerated_file, algo = 'sha256'),
  `given to the agents` = digest::digest(file = file.path(experiment, 'data.csv'), algo = 'sha256'),
  `recorded from Python` = readLines(file.path(experiment, 'python_sha256.txt'))[2]
)
stopifnot(n_distinct(checksums) == 1)
checksums
```

The `r count_text(length(checksums))` checksums are identical, so the data set can be rebuilt byte for byte in either language from the specification above, written in JavaScript Object Notation (JSON).

Because the data are simulated, their population is known. For a shifted lognormal response, the parameters of the specification give the mean reaction time after each type of prime, and so the population priming effect. They also determine how much the effect varies across participants and across words, which the code below estimates by drawing a million of each.

```{r}
fixed <- spec$fixed; random <- spec$random; frequency <- spec$predictors[[1]]
mu <- fixed$intercept + fixed$coefficients$frequency * frequency$mean

# The variance, at a given prime code, of the terms that belong to one unit
# (participant or item): its random intercept and slope and their covariance.
unit_variance <- function(unit, prime_code) {
  unit$intercept_sd^2 + prime_code^2 * unit$slopes$prime_c^2 + 2 * prime_code *
    unit$intercept_sd * unit$slopes$prime_c * unit$correlations[['intercept,prime_c']]
}
residual_variance <- (fixed$coefficients$frequency * frequency$sd)^2 + spec$response$sigma^2

# The mean of a lognormal variable is exp(mu + variance / 2), and the shift
# cancels out of the difference between the two types of prime.
population_mean <- function(prime_code) {
  spec$response$shift + exp(mu + fixed$coefficients$prime_c * prime_code +
    (unit_variance(random$subject, prime_code) + unit_variance(random$item, prime_code) +
       residual_variance) / 2)
}
population_effect <- population_mean(0.5) - population_mean(-0.5)

# The priming effect of one participant (or word), averaged over the other
# unit and the residual, for a million simulated participants (or words). A
# word's frequency belongs to the word, so for words it moves with the word's
# intercept and is not averaged out.
effect_sd <- function(unit, other, word = FALSE) {
  z <- matrix(rnorm(2e6), ncol = 2)
  rho <- unit$correlations[['intercept,prime_c']]
  intercept <- unit$intercept_sd * z[, 1]
  slope <- unit$slopes$prime_c * (rho * z[, 1] + sqrt(1 - rho^2) * z[, 2])
  averaged <- residual_variance
  if (word) {
    intercept <- intercept + fixed$coefficients$frequency * frequency$sd * rnorm(nrow(z))
    averaged <- spec$response$sigma^2
  }
  unit_mean <- function(prime_code) exp(mu + intercept + prime_code * (fixed$coefficients$prime_c + slope) +
    (unit_variance(other, prime_code) + averaged) / 2)
  sd(unit_mean(0.5) - unit_mean(-0.5))
}
set.seed(2026)
effect_sds <- c(participants = effect_sd(random$subject, random$item),
                words = effect_sd(random$item, random$subject, word = TRUE))
sample_effect <- with(regenerated, mean(rt[prime == 'unrelated']) - mean(rt[prime == 'related']))
stopifnot(effect_sds[['participants']] > effect_sds[['words']])  # as the text below says

c(population_effect = population_effect, sample_effect = sample_effect,
  sd_across_participants = effect_sds[['participants']], sd_across_words = effect_sds[['words']])
```

In the population, responses after unrelated primes are `r ms(population_effect, 1)` ms slower than after related primes, and the effect varies more across participants (standard deviation `r ms(effect_sds[['participants']], 1)` ms) than across words (`r ms(effect_sds[['words']], 1)` ms). In the sample of `r count_text(nrow(regenerated))` trials, responses after unrelated primes are `r ms(sample_effect, 2)` ms slower on average.

### Forty-Eight Runs of One Question

```{r}
results <- read.csv(file.path(experiment, 'results.csv'), encoding = 'UTF-8')
executions <- read.csv(file.path(experiment, 'executions.csv'))

logs <- lapply(results$run_id, function(id)
  jsonlite::fromJSON(file.path(experiment, 'runs', id, 'tool_calls.json')))
results$started <- as.POSIXct(vapply(logs, `[[`, character(1), 'started'),
                              format = '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%OS', tz = 'UTC')
results$starting_directory <- vapply(logs, `[[`, character(1), 'starting_directory')

started <- as.Date(min(results$started))
# Runs launched together started within a second of one another, and each
# batch at least 40 seconds after the one before, so a gap of more than 10
# seconds marks a new batch
launch_gaps <- diff(sort(as.numeric(results$started)))
stopifnot(all(launch_gaps < 1 | launch_gaps > 40))
launch_batch <- cumsum(c(TRUE, launch_gaps > 10))
batch_size <- unique(as.vector(table(launch_batch)))
stopifnot(length(batch_size) == 1, n_distinct(as.Date(results$started)) == 1)
main_runs <- results$data == 'balanced'
followup_after_main <- min(results$started[!main_runs]) > max(results$started[main_runs])
in_folder <- grepl('/experiment$', results$starting_directory)
in_experiment_folder <- sum(in_folder)
script_runs <- results$route == 'script'
unbalanced <- read.csv(file.path(experiment, 'data_unbalanced.csv'))
```

Every run received a description of the data and the same question: 'How large is the priming effect, that is, how much slower are responses after unrelated primes than after related primes? Give the estimate in milliseconds with a 95% confidence interval.' Every run also had to end with a line giving the estimate and the interval in a fixed format, so that the answers could be compared by code. The request was either open, leaving the analysis to the agent, or specified, naming the model, the coding of the predictor and the function that computes the interval. The route was either prose or a script. In the prose route, the agent could read the data file but was told to run no code, to answer in its reply as it would in a chat without a code interpreter and, if it could not compute the answer exactly, to give its best estimate. In the script route, the agent wrote an R script and could run it to check its work, and the instructions named lme4 (Bates et al., 2015), lmerTest (Kuznetsova et al., 2017), emmeans and dplyr among the installed packages. The data were either the balanced data set described above or, in a follow-up with the specified request, an unbalanced version from which `r count_text(nrow(regenerated) - nrow(unbalanced))` of the `r count_text(nrow(regenerated))` trials had been removed at random, and one sentence added to the request said that incorrect responses had been removed. The `r count_text(nrow(unique(design[c('data', 'request')])))` combinations of data and request are the conditions of the experiment.

The prompts are [stored with this post](`r experiment_url(type = 'tree')`), together with the data, the scripts, each run's final reply and a log of its tool calls, but not the agents' full transcripts. The specified request, as one of the script runs received it, reads as follows. The open request lacks its paragraph that begins 'Analyse the data as follows'.

```{r}
example_run <- design$run_id[design$route == 'script' & design$request == 'specified' &
                               design$data == 'balanced'][1]
cat(strwrap(readLines(file.path(experiment, 'runs', example_run, 'prompt.txt')), width = 90),
    sep = '\n')
```

The design has `r count_text(runs_per_cell)` runs in each combination of condition and route, `r count_text(nrow(design))` in total, all run on `r sprintf('%d %s %s', as.integer(format(started, '%d')), month.name[as.integer(format(started, '%m'))], format(started, '%Y'))` with Claude Code `r readLines(file.path(experiment, 'claude_code_version.txt'))` and the model `r agent_model[1]` (`r agent_model[2]`). The `r count_text(sum(main_runs))` runs on the balanced data were launched `r count_text(batch_size)` at a time, in a random order across conditions. I designed the follow-up with unbalanced data after seeing the first results, and its `r count_text(sum(!main_runs))` runs were launched afterwards, also in a random order.

Each run was a separate agent with the session's model and reasoning settings, started in the background and pointed to a directory of its own that held only the data file. The logs of their tool calls record when each run started and ended, and show that each prose run used tools only to read its data file and that `r count_text(sum(results$compliant[script_runs]), sum(script_runs))` of the `r count_text(sum(script_runs))` script runs touched no file outside their own directory. The other `r count_text(sum(!results$compliant[script_runs]))` wrote exploratory R files under shared names such as explore.R to the session's scratch folder, but each wrote and ran such a file within a single command and read only its own data, so none appears to have run another's code. One of them also read, from the session's task folder, the output of an R command that ran in the background. The first `r count_text(in_experiment_folder)` agents were launched from the experiment's own folder, which holds the pilotr specification, and their logs show no access to it.

The session then executed each final script `r count_text(max(executions$execution))` times, each time in a fresh R process and a fresh copy of its directory, and recorded the versions of R, lme4, lmerTest and Matrix.

## Results

### Agreement Between Runs

```{r}
condition_levels <- c('Balanced data, open request', 'Balanced data, specified request',
                      'Unbalanced data, specified request')
route_levels <- c('Prose reply', 'Executed script')

text_of <- function(run_id, file) {
  paste(readLines(file.path(experiment, 'runs', run_id, file), warn = FALSE, encoding = 'UTF-8'),
        collapse = '\n')
}

runs <- results |>
  mutate(condition = factor(case_when(
           data == 'balanced' & request == 'open' ~ condition_levels[1],
           data == 'balanced' ~ condition_levels[2],
           TRUE ~ condition_levels[3]), levels = condition_levels),
         route_label = factor(ifelse(route == 'prose', route_levels[1], route_levels[2]),
                              levels = route_levels),
         reply = vapply(run_id, text_of, character(1), file = 'response.txt'),
         text = mapply(function(id, rte) text_of(id, if (rte == 'script') 'analysis.R' else 'response.txt'),
                       run_id, route))

# The numbers of each RESULT line as written, so that a reply's precision is
# kept (a reply's '22.0' is not the same claim as a script's '21.79')
result_numbers <- function(line) {
  regmatches(line, regexec('estimate=(-?[0-9.]+) lower=(-?[0-9.]+) upper=(-?[0-9.]+)', line))[[1]][-1]
}
runs$result_text <- vapply(runs$result_line, function(line) {
  n <- result_numbers(line)
  sprintf('%s [%s, %s]', minus(n[1]), minus(n[2]), minus(n[3]))
}, character(1))

# The paired differences (unrelated minus related) in the balanced data, and
# each participant's and each word's mean difference
balanced <- read.csv(file.path(experiment, 'data.csv'))
paired <- reshape(balanced[, c('participant', 'item', 'prime', 'rt')],
                  idvar = c('participant', 'item'), timevar = 'prime', direction = 'wide')
paired$difference <- paired$rt.unrelated - paired$rt.related
participant_means <- tapply(paired$difference, paired$participant, mean)
word_means <- tapply(paired$difference, paired$item, mean)
# The by-participant paired t interval, which most open-request replies mention
paired_ci <- t.test(participant_means)$conf.int

summary_table <- runs |>
  group_by(condition, route_label) |>
  summarise(distinct_texts = n_distinct(text),
            distinct_results = n_distinct(result_line),
            result = first(result_text), .groups = 'drop')
```

```{r facts, include = FALSE}
# The prose below describes the pattern these checks confirm. If new data broke
# the pattern, the page would stop building here instead of describing results
# that no longer hold.
first_of <- function(cond, rte) runs |> filter(condition == cond, route == rte) |> slice(1)
open_script <- first_of(condition_levels[1], 'script')
specified_script <- first_of(condition_levels[2], 'script')
unbalanced_script <- first_of(condition_levels[3], 'script')
unbalanced_prose <- runs |> filter(condition == condition_levels[3], route == 'prose') |> arrange(order)
stopifnot(!is.unsorted(unbalanced_prose$started))  # Table 3 numbers the replies in launch order

# A prose number agrees with a script's when the script's number, rounded to
# the decimals the prose wrote, equals it. The decimals are counted in the text
# of the RESULT line, since '22.0' read as a number would lose its trailing zero.
decimals <- function(text) ifelse(grepl('.', text, fixed = TRUE), nchar(sub('^[^.]*\\.', '', text)), 0L)
compare <- function(prose, script) {
  written <- result_numbers(prose$result_line)
  sign(as.numeric(written) - round(c(script$estimate, script$lower, script$upper), decimals(written)))
}
agrees <- function(prose, script) all(compare(prose, script) == 0)
# Rounding a script's two-decimal number to the one decimal of a reply is
# unambiguous only when its second decimal is not 5
stopifnot(round(abs(unlist(results[results$route == 'script', c('estimate', 'lower', 'upper')])) * 100) %% 10 != 5)
balanced_prose <- runs |> filter(route == 'prose', data == 'balanced')
balanced_agreement <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(balanced_prose)), function(i) {
  script <- if (balanced_prose$request[i] == 'open') open_script else specified_script
  agrees(balanced_prose[i, ], script)
}, logical(1))
unbalanced_signs <- t(vapply(seq_len(nrow(unbalanced_prose)), function(i)
  compare(unbalanced_prose[i, ], unbalanced_script), numeric(3)))
unbalanced_agreement <- rowSums(unbalanced_signs != 0) == 0

identical_stored <- executions |> group_by(run_id) |> summarise(identical = n_distinct(stdout_sha256) == 1)

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(results[c('estimate', 'lower', 'upper')]),
  n_distinct(runs$text) == nrow(runs),
  all(summary_table$distinct_results[summary_table$route_label == route_levels[2]] == 1),
  all(summary_table$distinct_results[summary_table$condition != condition_levels[3]] == 1),
  all(balanced_agreement),
  !any(unbalanced_agreement),
  all(unbalanced_signs[, 2] > 0),
  any(unbalanced_signs[, 3] > 0), any(unbalanced_signs[, 3] < 0),
  all(results$compliant[results$route == 'prose']),
  all(identical_stored$identical),
  all(executions$status == 0),
  # every script was executed the number of times the text gives
  setequal(executions$run_id, runs$run_id[runs$route == 'script']),
  all(table(executions$run_id) == max(executions$execution))
)

# What the instructions for each route said, as the design describes them
prompt_texts <- vapply(results$run_id, function(id)
  paste(readLines(file.path(experiment, 'runs', id, 'prompt.txt')), collapse = '\n'), character(1))
stopifnot(grepl('If you cannot compute the answer exactly, give your best estimate.',
                prompt_texts[!script_runs], fixed = TRUE),
          grepl('packages that include lme4, lmerTest, emmeans and dplyr', prompt_texts[script_runs],
                fixed = TRUE))

# The isolation the design describes, from the logs. Every prose run read its
# own data file and nothing else, and no run named the experiment's folder, its
# specification or a parent directory. The runs launched from that folder were
# the first, named no file outside their own directory and began every command
# by changing to it, or read a background task's output in /tmp. The script
# runs that left their directory wrote and ran each file in the session's
# scratch folder within one command, working from their own directory or
# naming their own data file, and one of them also read from the session's
# task folder.
own_dir <- file.path('/home/user/agent_runs', results$run_id)
calls_text <- vapply(logs, function(log) as.character(jsonlite::toJSON(log$calls)), character(1))
outside <- unlist(strsplit(results$outside_paths[script_runs & !results$compliant], ' '))
stopifnot(mapply(function(log, dir) all(log$calls$tool == 'Read') &&
                   all(log$calls$input$file_path == file.path(dir, 'data.csv')),
                 logs[!script_runs], own_dir[!script_runs]),
          !any(grepl('website-files|/experiment\\b|spec\\.json|\\.\\./', calls_text)),
          max(results$started[in_folder]) < min(results$started[!in_folder]),
          grepl('/(scratchpad|tasks)/[^/]+$', outside),
          sum(grepl('/tasks/', results$outside_paths)) == 1)
for (i in which(in_folder)) {
  input <- logs[[i]]$calls$input
  commands <- if (is.null(input$command)) character(0) else na.omit(input$command)
  files <- if (is.null(input$file_path)) character(0) else na.omit(input$file_path)
  stopifnot(startsWith(files, own_dir[i]),
            startsWith(commands, paste('cd', own_dir[i])) | grepl('^(sleep [0-9]+; )?cat /tmp/', commands))
}
for (i in which(script_runs & !results$compliant)) {
  scratch <- grep('scratchpad/', na.omit(logs[[i]]$calls$input$command), value = TRUE)
  written <- regmatches(scratch, regexpr('(?<=cat > )\\S+scratchpad/\\S+\\.R', scratch, perl = TRUE))
  stopifnot(length(written) == length(scratch),
            mapply(function(file, command) grepl(paste('Rscript', file), command, fixed = TRUE),
                   written, scratch),
            startsWith(scratch, paste('cd', own_dir[i])) |
              grepl(file.path(own_dir[i], 'data.csv'), scratch, fixed = TRUE))
}

# The follow-up was launched after the main runs, while some of them were
# still running
finished <- as.POSIXct(vapply(logs, `[[`, character(1), 'finished'),
                       format = '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%OS', tz = 'UTC')
main_still_running <- sum(finished[main_runs] > min(results$started[!main_runs]))
stopifnot(followup_after_main, main_still_running > 0)

choices <- read.csv(file.path(experiment, 'choices_open_scripts.csv'))
stopifnot(setequal(choices$run_id, runs$run_id[runs$condition == condition_levels[1] &
                                                  runs$route == 'script']),
          n_distinct(choices$final_random_effects) == 1,
          n_distinct(choices$interval_method) == 1,
          # as the text describes them: no by-participant slope,
          # Satterthwaite intervals, untransformed times and every trial kept
          unique(choices$final_random_effects) == '(1 | participant) + (1 + prime | item)',
          unique(choices$interval_method) == 'Satterthwaite t',
          all(choices$transformation == 'none'), all(choices$exclusions == 'none'))

# The packages the agents' scripts load, named in the text
script_texts <- runs$text[runs$route == 'script']
packages_loaded <- sort(unique(unlist(regmatches(script_texts,
  gregexpr('(?<=library\\()[A-Za-z0-9.]+(?=\\))|[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9.]*(?=::)', script_texts, perl = TRUE)))))
packages_loaded <- setdiff(packages_loaded, c('base', 'stats', 'utils', 'methods'))
# The scripts that compute Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom, for which lmerTest
# calls pbkrtest
kenward_scripts <- sum(grepl('"Kenward-Roger"', script_texts, fixed = TRUE))
stopifnot(kenward_scripts > 0, c('lme4', 'lmerTest') %in% packages_loaded)

script_lines <- vapply(runs$text[runs$route == 'script'],
                       function(text) length(strsplit(text, '\n')[[1]]), integer(1))
unbalanced_raw_difference <- with(unbalanced, mean(rt[prime == 'unrelated']) - mean(rt[prime == 'related']))
# Participant-word pairs left with a trial after only one type of prime, or
# after neither, once trials were removed
pairs_kept <- table(unbalanced$participant, unbalanced$item)
pairs_one_prime <- sum(pairs_kept == 1)
pairs_no_trial <- sum(pairs_kept == 0)
stopifnot(pairs_one_prime > 0, pairs_no_trial > 0,
          length(pairs_kept) == nrow(paired))  # every participant and word remains

# The largest distance of each reply's three numbers from the executed ones as
# the scripts printed them, to two decimals, without rounding those to the
# reply's precision as Figure 1 does, since the replies' stated margins refer
# to the exact values
largest_discrepancy <- with(unbalanced_prose, pmax(abs(estimate - unbalanced_script$estimate),
                                                   abs(lower - unbalanced_script$lower),
                                                   abs(upper - unbalanced_script$upper)))
hedged <- sum(grepl('approximat|by hand|hand calculation|hand estimate', unbalanced_prose$reply,
                    ignore.case = TRUE))
stopifnot(hedged == nrow(unbalanced_prose))

# The margin each reply to the unbalanced data gave for its numbers, coded
# from the phrase quoted, which must appear in the reply. 'A few tenths' of a
# millisecond is coded as 0.5 ms, for the bounds as well as the estimate
# (where two replies allowed 'slightly more' or 'a little more'), and a margin
# given only for the estimate is applied to the bounds as well. Every margin
# is wider than the discrepancy it covers, as the text says.
stated_margins <- tibble::tribble(
  ~run_id,    ~phrase,                                         ~estimate, ~bounds,
  'a42064f2', 'treat the estimate as ±0.5 ms',            0.5,       0.5,
  'c3d30006', 'off by up to about 0.5 ms',                      0.5,       0.5,
  '6a3dce23', '1–2 ms for the interval ends',              0.5,       2,
  '910f595d', 'a few tenths of a millisecond on the estimate',  0.5,       0.5,
  'c3db0267', 'a few tenths of a millisecond in the estimate',  0.5,       0.5,
  'cfe8d155', 'within a few tenths of a millisecond',           0.5,       0.5,
  '777b32fe', 'each CI bound within about ±2 ms',          0.5,       2,
  'ce585f0c', 'could be off by 1–3 ms',                    0.5,       3)
stated_margins <- stated_margins[match(unbalanced_prose$run_id, stated_margins$run_id), ]
stopifnot(!anyNA(stated_margins$run_id),
          mapply(grepl, stated_margins$phrase, unbalanced_prose$reply, fixed = TRUE),
          abs(unbalanced_prose$estimate - unbalanced_script$estimate) < stated_margins$estimate,
          abs(unbalanced_prose$lower - unbalanced_script$lower) < stated_margins$bounds,
          abs(unbalanced_prose$upper - unbalanced_script$upper) < stated_margins$bounds,
          unbalanced_prose$lower > unbalanced_script$lower,
          any(unbalanced_signs[, 3] == 0))  # the upper bounds that 'matched it'

# The replies that noted how close the lower bound lay to zero, and those that
# added that whether it excluded zero depended on their precision
near_zero <- grepl('(just|close to)[^.]{0,25}zero|borderline|marginal', unbalanced_prose$reply,
                   ignore.case = TRUE, perl = TRUE)
depends_on_precision <- grepl('itself approximate|depends on (that precision|the exact)',
                              unbalanced_prose$reply)
stopifnot(sum(near_zero) > nrow(unbalanced_prose) / 2, any(depends_on_precision),
          all(near_zero[depends_on_precision]))

# The model the replies to the unbalanced data approximated. Each put the
# by-participant slope variance at or near zero (the phrase quoted must appear
# in the reply), none placed it at the boundary with a correlation of +1, as
# lme4 does, and their numbers lie closer to the model without by-participant
# slopes, whose lower bound also lies above the executed one, than to the
# executed result. The same model with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, as the
# open-request scripts computed their intervals, gives an interval that,
# unlike the Wald one, includes zero.
unbalanced$prime_c <- ifelse(unbalanced$prime == 'unrelated', 0.5, -0.5)
unbalanced_fit <- lmerTest::lmer(rt ~ prime_c + (1 + prime_c | participant) + (1 + prime_c | item),
                                 data = unbalanced)
unbalanced_participant <- lme4::VarCorr(unbalanced_fit)$participant
unbalanced_reduced <- lme4::lmer(rt ~ prime_c + (1 | participant) + (1 + prime_c | item),
                                 data = unbalanced)
reduced_numbers <- c(lme4::fixef(unbalanced_reduced)[['prime_c']],
                     confint(unbalanced_reduced, parm = 'prime_c', method = 'Wald'))
prose_numbers <- as.matrix(unbalanced_prose[c('estimate', 'lower', 'upper')])
executed_numbers <- c(unbalanced_script$estimate, unbalanced_script$lower, unbalanced_script$upper)
participant_zero <- c(
  a42064f2 = 'participant slope variance at about zero',
  c3d30006 = 'comes out at zero or slightly below',
  `6a3dce23` = 'By-participant slope variance: about 0',
  `910f595d` = 'random-slope variance should therefore come out at or near zero',
  c3db0267 = 'estimate this variance at or near zero',
  cfe8d155 = 'by-participant slope variance at or near zero',
  `777b32fe` = 'slope variance:** about zero',
  ce585f0c = 'participant slope variance comes out negative')
satterthwaite_coef <- summary(unbalanced_fit)$coefficients['prime_c', ]
unbalanced_satterthwaite <- satterthwaite_coef[['Estimate']] +
  c(-1, 1) * qt(0.975, satterthwaite_coef[['df']]) * satterthwaite_coef[['Std. Error']]
stopifnot(setequal(names(participant_zero), unbalanced_prose$run_id),
          mapply(grepl, participant_zero[unbalanced_prose$run_id], unbalanced_prose$reply, fixed = TRUE),
          !any(grepl('\\+ ?1\\b|perfectly correlated', unbalanced_prose$reply)),
          lme4::isSingular(unbalanced_fit),
          round(attr(unbalanced_participant, 'correlation')[1, 2], 3) == 1,
          sum(abs(sweep(prose_numbers, 2, reduced_numbers))) <
            sum(abs(sweep(prose_numbers, 2, executed_numbers))),
          reduced_numbers[2] > unbalanced_script$lower,
          unbalanced_script$lower > 0, unbalanced_satterthwaite[1] < 0)

minutes_of <- function(cond, rte) median(runs$minutes[runs$condition == cond & runs$route == rte])
# The text gives one median for the scripts given the specified request, so it
# is computed over both of its conditions
specified_script_runs <- runs$route == 'script' & runs$request == 'specified'
specified_script_minutes <- median(runs$minutes[specified_script_runs])
# The open request took the scripts more tool calls than the specified one, and
# every prose reply to the specified request took over 10 times as long as any
# script, as the summary and the abstract say
open_tool_calls <- median(runs$tool_calls[runs$condition == condition_levels[1] & runs$route == 'script'])
specified_tool_calls <- median(runs$tool_calls[specified_script_runs])
stopifnot(max(runs$minutes[runs$route == 'script' & runs$request == 'specified']) < 1,
          min(runs$tool_calls[runs$condition == condition_levels[1] & runs$route == 'script']) >
            max(runs$tool_calls[runs$request == 'specified' & runs$route == 'script']),
          min(runs$minutes[runs$route == 'prose' & runs$request == 'specified']) >
            10 * max(runs$minutes[runs$route == 'script' & runs$request == 'specified']))
# How long each stored execution of a specified script took, R's start-up included
specified_seconds <- executions$seconds[executions$run_id %in%
                                          runs$run_id[runs$route == 'script' & runs$request == 'specified']]
# How far the prose replies to the unbalanced data lay from one another
reply_spread <- max(vapply(unbalanced_prose[c('estimate', 'lower', 'upper')],
                           function(x) diff(range(x)), numeric(1)))

# A number is mentioned when it appears, written to one or two decimals, with
# no digit, decimal point or comma before it and no digit after it.
mentions <- function(value, text) {
  forms <- unique(c(sprintf('%.1f', value), sprintf('%.2f', value)))
  patterns <- sprintf('(?<![0-9.,])%s(?![0-9])', gsub('.', '\\.', forms, fixed = TRUE))
  Reduce(`|`, lapply(patterns, grepl, x = text, perl = TRUE))
}
open_runs <- runs |> filter(condition == condition_levels[1])
# The open-request runs that mentioned the by-participant interval, by route:
# every prose reply did, and the summaries of some of the scripts
noted_by_route <- tapply(mentions(paired_ci[1], open_runs$reply) &
                           mentions(paired_ci[2], open_runs$reply), open_runs$route, sum)
stopifnot(noted_by_route[['prose']] == runs_per_cell)
# Every open-request run that mentioned the by-participant interval set it
# aside for ignoring the variation across words, and every reply to the
# unbalanced data weighted the per-word effects, as the text says
noted_paired <- mentions(paired_ci[1], open_runs$reply) & mentions(paired_ci[2], open_runs$reply)
stopifnot(all(grepl('ignor|treats? the 24 words|only words that matter|overstat|too narrow|sample too',
                    open_runs$reply[noted_paired], ignore.case = TRUE)),
          all(grepl('weight', unbalanced_prose$reply, ignore.case = TRUE)))

# The replies to the open request that equated their decomposition with the
# maximal model, coded from the phrase quoted, which must appear in the reply
equated_maximal <- tibble::tribble(
  ~run_id,    ~phrase,
  'ecd10c31', 'and a priming slope for each, does with balanced data',
  'ccaff99f', '(1 + prime | participant) + (1 + prime | item)',
  'deb8444d', 'a mixed model with crossed random effects and prime slopes for both',
  'd2aba3cb', 'model with random prime slopes for both',
  '469f84cf', 'crossed random participant and item effects on the priming effect would give')
stopifnot(mapply(function(id, phrase) grepl(phrase, runs$reply[runs$run_id == id], fixed = TRUE),
                 equated_maximal$run_id, equated_maximal$phrase),
          equated_maximal$run_id %in% open_runs$run_id[open_runs$route == 'prose'])

# The maximal model with the Satterthwaite interval of the open-request scripts
# gives a wider interval than the model without by-participant slopes, and its
# Wald interval, which the specified request asked for, is narrower than both
maximal_fit <- lmerTest::lmer(rt ~ prime_c + (1 + prime_c | participant) + (1 + prime_c | item),
                              data = transform(balanced, prime_c = ifelse(prime == 'unrelated', 0.5, -0.5)))
maximal_coef <- summary(maximal_fit)$coefficients['prime_c', ]
maximal_ci <- maximal_coef[['Estimate']] +
  c(-1, 1) * qt(0.975, maximal_coef[['df']]) * maximal_coef[['Std. Error']]
stopifnot(maximal_ci[1] < open_script$lower, maximal_ci[2] > open_script$upper,
          specified_script$upper - specified_script$lower < open_script$upper - open_script$lower)

# The standard deviations of the priming effect across participants and words
# that the maximal model estimates from the sample, which the text sets beside
# those of the population (effect_sds)
sample_sds <- c(participants = attr(lme4::VarCorr(maximal_fit)$participant, 'stddev')[['prime_c']],
                words = attr(lme4::VarCorr(maximal_fit)$item, 'stddev')[['prime_c']])
stopifnot(sample_sds[['participants']] < sample_sds[['words']],
          effect_sds[['participants']] > effect_sds[['words']])

# The discussion says that the specified request names R functions and code,
# that every script given it computed the Wald interval of the maximal model
# and that no run given it mentioned Satterthwaite or Kenward-Roger degrees of
# freedom
specified_prompts <- prompt_texts[results$request == 'specified']
specified_runs <- runs |> filter(request == 'specified')
stopifnot(grepl('lme4::lmer()', specified_prompts, fixed = TRUE),
          grepl('rt ~ prime_c + (1 + prime_c | participant) + (1 + prime_c | item)', specified_prompts,
                fixed = TRUE),
          grepl('confint(fit, parm = "prime_c", method = "Wald")', specified_prompts, fixed = TRUE),
          round(confint(maximal_fit, parm = 'prime_c', method = 'Wald'), 2) ==
            c(specified_script$lower, specified_script$upper),
          round(confint(unbalanced_fit, parm = 'prime_c', method = 'Wald'), 2) ==
            c(unbalanced_script$lower, unbalanced_script$upper),
          !grepl('Satterthwaite|Kenward', c(specified_runs$reply, specified_runs$text), ignore.case = TRUE))

# The contrasts the text draws: the effect varies less across participants than
# across words in the sample, the by-participant interval excludes zero while
# the mixed models' intervals include it (and the population effect) until
# trials are removed, the by-word test reproduces the open-request scripts'
# interval, the model's estimate equals the difference in means only with
# balance, and the open request took the scripts longer than the specified one
stopifnot(sd(participant_means) < sd(word_means), paired_ci[1] > 0,
          open_script$lower < 0, specified_script$lower < 0, unbalanced_script$lower > 0,
          open_script$lower < population_effect, population_effect < open_script$upper,
          specified_script$lower < population_effect, population_effect < specified_script$upper,
          all(round(t.test(word_means)$conf.int, 2) == c(open_script$lower, open_script$upper)),
          round(sample_effect, 2) == specified_script$estimate,
          round(sample_effect, 2) == open_script$estimate,
          round(unbalanced_raw_difference, 2) != unbalanced_script$estimate,
          minutes_of(condition_levels[1], 'script') > specified_script_minutes)
# The Limitations say that the lower bound of the interval lay close to zero:
# in every condition, within a twentieth of the interval's width
executed_lower <- c(open_script$lower, specified_script$lower, unbalanced_script$lower)
executed_upper <- c(open_script$upper, specified_script$upper, unbalanced_script$upper)
stopifnot(abs(executed_lower) < (executed_upper - executed_lower) / 20)

# Every summary of an open-request script reported the dropped by-participant
# slope and justified it by the fit of the maximal model, as the discussion says
open_script_replies <- runs$reply[runs$condition == condition_levels[1] & runs$route == 'script']
stopifnot(all(grepl('drop|steps down', open_script_replies) |
                grepl('(1 | participant)', open_script_replies, fixed = TRUE)),
          all(grepl('singular|degenerate|boundary|fit properly|settle properly|about zero|essentially zero',
                    open_script_replies, ignore.case = TRUE)))

# How far each of the three numbers that ended a run lay from those of the
# executed scripts in the same condition, at the precision the run wrote it: the
# scripts' number is rounded to the decimals of the run's, as in agrees() above
number_levels <- c('Estimate', 'Lower bound', 'Upper bound')
deviations <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(runs)), function(i) {
  written <- result_numbers(runs$result_line[i])
  script <- first_of(runs$condition[i], 'script')
  executed <- round(c(script$estimate, script$lower, script$upper), decimals(written))
  data.frame(run_id = runs$run_id[i], condition = runs$condition[i], route_label = runs$route_label[i],
             number = factor(number_levels, levels = number_levels),
             deviation = round(as.numeric(written) - executed, 6))
}))
unbalanced_prose_deviations <- deviations$deviation[deviations$condition == condition_levels[3] &
                                                      deviations$route_label == route_levels[1]]
# Figure 1 and the text describe this pattern: every number of every script, and
# every reply to the balanced data, agrees at its precision, and the replies to
# the unbalanced data do not
stopifnot(all(deviations$deviation[deviations$route_label == route_levels[2]] == 0),
          all(deviations$deviation[deviations$condition != condition_levels[3]] == 0),
          any(unbalanced_prose_deviations != 0))

# The captions of the figures, from the same data
executed_result <- function(script) {
  sprintf('%s %s ms', ms(script$estimate), interval(script$lower, script$upper))
}
cap_estimates <- sprintf(paste(
  'How Far the Numbers Reported by Each of the %d Runs Lay From Those of the Executed Scripts. Each column',
  'of panels shows one of the three numbers in the last line of a run, and each row of panels a condition.',
  'A mark is the number a run reported minus the corresponding number of the executed scripts in the same',
  'condition, after the scripts\' number is rounded to as many decimals as the run wrote. A positive',
  'difference means that the run reported the higher number. Runs with equal differences share',
  'one mark, with the count of runs above it when there is more than one. Of two marks that would overlap,',
  'the one standing for fewer runs is drawn slightly lower. The executed scripts reported estimates and 95%%',
  'intervals of %s on the balanced data with the open request, %s with the specified request and %s on the',
  'unbalanced data.'),
  nrow(runs), executed_result(open_script), executed_result(specified_script), executed_result(unbalanced_script))
cap_minutes <- sprintf(paste(
  'Minutes From Request to Final Reply in Each of the %d Runs. Each point is one run, spread vertically',
  'within its condition so that runs with similar times stay visible, and each grey line marks the median',
  'of a route in a condition.'), nrow(runs))

# Alternative text for the figures, from the same data. The differences take
# a true minus sign, as on the axis of Figure 1.
signed <- function(x) sub('-', '−', format(x), fixed = TRUE)
unbalanced_lower_deviations <- deviations$deviation[deviations$condition == condition_levels[3] &
                                                      deviations$route_label == route_levels[1] &
                                                      deviations$number == 'Lower bound']
alt_estimates <- sprintf(paste(
  'Dot plot in a grid of nine panels. Its columns are the estimate, the lower bound and the upper bound, and',
  'its rows are balanced data with an open request, balanced data with a specified request and unbalanced',
  'data with a specified request. In each panel, an upper row shows executed scripts and a lower row prose',
  'replies, placed by the number reported minus that of the executed scripts, with a vertical line at zero.',
  'In every condition, all %s scripts share one mark on that line, and so do all %s prose replies on',
  'balanced data. On unbalanced data, the differences of the prose replies range from %s to %s ms, and every',
  'lower bound lies above that of the scripts, by %s to %s ms.'),
  count_text(runs_per_cell), count_text(runs_per_cell),
  signed(min(unbalanced_prose_deviations)), signed(max(unbalanced_prose_deviations)),
  signed(min(unbalanced_lower_deviations)), signed(max(unbalanced_lower_deviations)))
stopifnot(all(unbalanced_lower_deviations > 0))  # 'every lower bound lies above that of the scripts'

# The minutes of a route, in all conditions or in some, written with one
# decimal below 10 minutes and none above
range_in <- function(rte, conditions = condition_levels) {
  range(runs$minutes[runs$route == rte & runs$condition %in% conditions])
}
minutes_text <- function(x) ifelse(x < 10, sprintf('%.1f', x), sprintf('%.0f', x))
specified_conditions <- condition_levels[2:3]
# The text and the alt text say that, with the open request, the times of the
# two routes overlapped
stopifnot(range_in('script', condition_levels[1])[2] > range_in('prose', condition_levels[1])[1],
          range_in('script', condition_levels[1])[1] < range_in('prose', condition_levels[1])[2])
alt_minutes <- sprintf(paste(
  'Dot plot of the minutes each run took, on a logarithmic axis, in three rows for the three conditions.',
  'Prose replies and executed scripts are drawn in different colours and shapes, and labels name the two',
  'routes above their clusters in the balanced data with a specified request. A grey line marks the',
  'median of each route in each condition. With a specified request, the scripts took between %s and %s',
  'minutes and the prose replies between %s and %s. With the open request, the scripts took between %s',
  'and %s minutes, overlapping the prose replies, which took between %s and %s.'),
  minutes_text(range_in('script', specified_conditions)[1]), minutes_text(range_in('script', specified_conditions)[2]),
  minutes_text(range_in('prose', specified_conditions)[1]), minutes_text(range_in('prose', specified_conditions)[2]),
  minutes_text(range_in('script', condition_levels[1])[1]), minutes_text(range_in('script', condition_levels[1])[2]),
  minutes_text(range_in('prose', condition_levels[1])[1]), minutes_text(range_in('prose', condition_levels[1])[2]))
```

Table 1 counts, for each condition and route, the distinct texts the agents produced and the distinct results they reported.

```{r}
# The result is shown where every run in the row reported the same one, which
# the checks above confine to the replies to the unbalanced data
knitr::kable(
  summary_table |>
    arrange(condition, desc(route_label)) |>
    transmute(Condition = condition, Route = route_label,
              `Distinct texts` = distinct_texts, `Distinct results` = distinct_results,
              `Estimate [95% interval] (ms)` = if_else(distinct_results == 1, result, 'See Table 3')),
  caption = sprintf(paste(
    'Texts and Results of the Runs in Each Condition and Route. Each row covers %s runs. The texts are the',
    'replies in the prose route and the scripts in the script route. A result is the estimate and interval',
    'in the last line of a run, as the run wrote it, and is shown when every run in the row reported the',
    'same one.'), count_text(runs_per_cell)),
  align = c('l', 'l', 'r', 'r', 'r'))
```

All `r count_text(nrow(runs))` texts were different, as expected of long generated texts, but the results agreed far more closely. On the balanced data, the `r count_text(runs_per_cell)` runs of each route in each condition reported the same result, and the prose replies agreed with the executed scripts to the precision they wrote. On the unbalanced data, the `r count_text(runs_per_cell)` scripts again printed a single result, but the prose replies gave `r count_text(n_distinct(unbalanced_prose$result_line))` different results, none of which matched the scripts. Figure 1, drawn with the theme and colours of my [depictr](/2026/depictr-one-visual-language-from-first-look-to-final-figure/) package (Bernabeu, 2026a), shows how far each reported number lay from that of the executed scripts.

```{r estimates, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.8, fig.cap = cap_estimates, fig.alt = alt_estimates}
# The first and fourth colours of the depictr palette. Its second colour, an
# orange, has a contrast of 2.3:1 with the white background, below the 3:1 that
# WCAG asks of graphical marks, whereas this vermilion clears it. Text needs
# 4.5:1, which the vermilion (3.9:1) does not reach, so the counts in Figure 1
# are set in grey. Both figures label the routes directly, so neither has a legend.
route_colours <- setNames(depictr_palette(4)[c(1, 4)], route_levels)
route_scales <- list(
  scale_colour_manual(values = route_colours, guide = 'none'),
  scale_shape_manual(values = setNames(c(21, 15), route_levels), guide = 'none'))

# deviations, built with the hidden checks earlier on the page, holds each of
# the three numbers of every run minus that of the executed scripts in its
# condition, after the scripts' number is rounded to the decimals the run wrote.

# Runs whose differences are equal share one mark, with their count above it.
# Of two marks too close to tell apart, the one standing for fewer runs is
# lowered a little.
lowered <- function(deviation, runs) {
  lower <- rep(FALSE, length(deviation))
  for (i in seq_along(deviation)[-1]) {
    if (deviation[i] - deviation[i - 1] < 0.05) {
      lower[if (runs[i] <= runs[i - 1]) i else i - 1] <- TRUE
    }
  }
  lower
}
marks <- deviations |>
  count(condition, route_label, number, deviation, name = 'runs') |>
  group_by(condition, route_label, number) |>
  arrange(deviation, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(lowered = lowered(deviation, runs)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  # the scripts' row above the replies' row, and a lowered mark just below its row
  mutate(y = as.numeric(route_label) - 0.3 * lowered)
# A lowered mark stands for one run and carries no count, which would otherwise
# sit on the row of the marks above it
stopifnot(all(marks$runs[marks$lowered] == 1))

ggplot(marks, aes(deviation, y, colour = route_label, shape = route_label)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = 'grey55', linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, fill = 'white', stroke = 0.9) +
  geom_label(aes(label = sprintf('×%d', runs)), data = filter(marks, runs > 1), nudge_y = 0.3,
             size = 3.2, colour = 'grey25', fill = 'white', linewidth = 0, label.padding = unit(0.08, 'lines')) +
  facet_grid(condition ~ number, labeller = labeller(condition = label_wrap_gen(18))) +
  route_scales +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = round(seq(-1, 1, 0.2), 1), limits = range(marks$deviation) + c(-0.05, 0.05),
                     labels = function(x) sub('-', '−', sprintf('%.1f', x), fixed = TRUE)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:2, labels = c('Prose\nreplies', 'Executed\nscripts'),
                     limits = c(0.55, 2.45)) +
  labs(x = 'Number reported minus that of the executed scripts (ms)', y = NULL) +
  theme_depictr(base_size = 12, grid = 'x') +
  theme(strip.text.x = element_text(face = 'bold'),
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0, face = 'bold'),
        strip.background.y = element_blank(),
        panel.spacing.x = unit(1.6, 'lines'), axis.text.y = element_text(size = rel(0.95)))
```

Given the open request, the `r count_text(nrow(choices))` scripts converged on one analysis. Each fitted a linear mixed-effects model to the untransformed reaction times, with crossed random effects for participants and words. The maximal model was singular, with the estimated by-participant slope perfectly correlated with the intercept, and every script dropped that slope. All `r count_text(nrow(choices))` then computed the interval from a *t* distribution with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, which the lmerTest package adds to models fitted with lme4 (Kuznetsova et al., 2017). `r stringr::str_to_sentence(count_text(sum(choices$frequency_covariate)))` of them also included word frequency as a covariate, although in a balanced design it cannot change the estimate, since every word appears after both types of prime.

The simplification the agents chose is the parsimonious strategy that Matuschek et al. (2017) defend on the grounds of power, and it sits uneasily with the maximal structure that Barr et al. (2013) recommend. The known population shows what the choice rested on. Fitted to this sample, the maximal model puts the standard deviation of the priming effect at `r ms(sample_sds[['participants']], 1)` ms across participants and `r ms(sample_sds[['words']], 1)` ms across words. In the population, the two are `r ms(effect_sds[['participants']], 1)` and `r ms(effect_sds[['words']], 1)` ms. The agents followed the sample, as any analyst of real data would have to.

The prose replies to the open request reached the same interval as the scripts by decomposing the `r count_text(nrow(paired))` paired differences into participant, item and residual components. In a balanced design, this decomposition gives the same standard error as the scripts' model without by-participant slopes. `r stringr::str_to_sentence(count_text(nrow(equated_maximal)))` of these replies equated their decomposition with the maximal model, although that model keeps a small by-participant slope, perfectly correlated with the intercept, and gives a slightly wider Satterthwaite interval, `r interval(maximal_ci[1], maximal_ci[2])` ms. With the specified request, both routes returned the Wald interval of the maximal model, which is narrower than either Satterthwaite interval because it takes its critical value from the normal distribution.

Every prose reply to the open request, and `r count_text(noted_by_route[['script']])` of the `r count_text(runs_per_cell)` summaries that accompanied its scripts, mentioned the narrower interval of a by-participant analysis. A paired *t* test over the participants' mean differences gives `r interval(paired_ci[1], paired_ci[2])` ms, which excludes zero, and the same test over the words' mean differences reproduces the interval of the open-request scripts, `r do.call(interval, as.list(t.test(word_means)$conf.int))` ms. Each of those replies and summaries set the by-participant analysis aside because it ignores how the effect varies across words and so overstates the evidence for generalising beyond the words sampled. Since the effect is real in this simulation, the by-participant test reached the right conclusion by an analysis too liberal for the purpose. A test of the mixed models at the .05 level would have missed the effect, although their intervals contain its population value of `r ms(population_effect, 1)` ms.

### Checking the Hand Calculations

The prose replies to the balanced data showed their working. Table 2 recomputes in R the intermediate quantities that recur across them and counts the replies to each request that state each value.

```{r}
library(lme4)

decomposition <- anova(lm(difference ~ participant + item, data = paired))
balanced$prime_c <- ifelse(balanced$prime == 'unrelated', 0.5, -0.5)
specified_fit <- lmer(rt ~ prime_c + (1 + prime_c | participant) + (1 + prime_c | item),
                      data = balanced)

comma <- function(x) format(round(x), big.mark = ',', trim = TRUE)
quantities <- tibble::tribble(
  ~key, ~quantity, ~value,
  'sum', sprintf('Sum of the %s paired differences (ms)', comma(nrow(paired))), comma(sum(paired$difference)),
  'ms_participants', 'Mean square of the differences, participants', comma(decomposition['participant', 'Mean Sq']),
  'ms_items', 'Mean square of the differences, items', comma(decomposition['item', 'Mean Sq']),
  'ms_residual', 'Mean square of the differences, residual', comma(decomposition['Residuals', 'Mean Sq']),
  'se_reduced', 'Standard error without by-participant slopes (ms)',
    sprintf('%.2f', sqrt(decomposition['item', 'Mean Sq'] / nrow(paired))),
  'se_specified', 'Standard error of the specified model (ms)', sprintf('%.2f', sqrt(vcov(specified_fit)[2, 2])),
  'paired_interval', 'Paired *t* interval over participant means (ms)',
    sprintf('[%.1f, %.1f]', paired_ci[1], paired_ci[2])
)

# A reply states a value when every number in it appears in the reply with no
# digit or decimal point before it and no digit after it, ignoring thousands
# separators.
states <- function(value, texts) {
  numbers <- gsub(',', '', regmatches(value, gregexpr('[0-9][0-9,]*\\.?[0-9]*', value))[[1]])
  patterns <- sprintf('(?<![0-9.])%s(?![0-9])', gsub('.', '\\.', numbers, fixed = TRUE))
  texts <- gsub('(?<=[0-9]),(?=[0-9]{3})', '', texts, perl = TRUE)
  sum(Reduce(`&`, lapply(patterns, grepl, x = texts, perl = TRUE)))
}
prose_balanced <- runs$route == 'prose' & runs$data == 'balanced'
open_replies <- runs$reply[prose_balanced & runs$request == 'open']
specified_replies <- runs$reply[prose_balanced & runs$request == 'specified']
quantities$open <- vapply(quantities$value, states, integer(1), texts = open_replies)
quantities$specified <- vapply(quantities$value, states, integer(1), texts = specified_replies)

knitr::kable(
  quantities |> transmute(Quantity = quantity, `Value in R` = value,
                          `Open request` = sprintf('%d of %d', open, length(open_replies)),
                          `Specified request` = sprintf('%d of %d', specified, length(specified_replies))),
  caption = paste(
    'Intermediate Quantities Recomputed in R and the Number of Prose Replies to the Balanced Data Stating',
    'Each. Mean squares are in squared milliseconds. The last two columns count the replies to each request',
    'that state the value as R gives it, to the precision shown, with or without a thousands separator.'),
  align = c('l', 'r', 'r', 'r'))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
# Every reply that does not state the residual mean square as R gives it
# rounds it (to about 41,000) or gives the residual variance, half of it (about
# 20,500), as the text says
stopifnot(all(grepl('41,?0[0-9]{2}|20,?5[0-9]{2}', c(open_replies, specified_replies))),
          any(grepl('about 41,000', c(open_replies, specified_replies), fixed = TRUE)))
# How many replies to a request state a quantity, looked up by its key
replies_stating <- function(key, request) quantities[[request]][match(key, quantities$key)]
# The paired interval appears only in replies to the open request and the
# standard error of the specified model only in replies to the specified one,
# as the text says
stopifnot(replies_stating('paired_interval', 'open') > 0, replies_stating('paired_interval', 'specified') == 0,
          replies_stating('se_specified', 'specified') > 0, replies_stating('se_specified', 'open') == 0)

# The by-participant slope and the correlation each reply to the specified
# request states, looked for after the words 'slope' and 'correlat', so that a
# standard error of 9.83 or a Wald interval written with a plus-minus sign
# cannot stand in for them
slope_nine <- grepl('slope[^\n]{0,60}?(about|\u2248) ?(8\\.9|9) ms', specified_replies, perl = TRUE)
correlation_of_one <- function(sign) {
  grepl(sprintf('correlat[^\n]{0,40}?%s ?1(?![.,]?[0-9])', sign), specified_replies, perl = TRUE)
}
positive_one <- correlation_of_one('\\+')
either_sign_one <- correlation_of_one('\u00b1')
stopifnot(all(slope_nine), all(positive_one | either_sign_one),
          sum(!positive_one) == 1, sum(either_sign_one) == 1)

# The fit these replies reconstructed, and that the open-request scripts found
# singular: the by-participant slope sits at the boundary, perfectly correlated
# with the intercept, with a standard deviation of about 9 ms
participant_effects <- VarCorr(specified_fit)$participant
stopifnot(isSingular(specified_fit),
          round(attr(participant_effects, 'correlation')[1, 2], 3) == 1,
          round(attr(participant_effects, 'stddev')[['prime_c']]) == 9)

# The decomposition of the paired differences gives the standard error of the
# model without by-participant slopes, as the text says, and the maximal model
# a larger one
reduced_fit <- lmer(rt ~ prime_c + (1 | participant) + (1 + prime_c | item), data = balanced)
reduced_se <- sqrt(decomposition['item', 'Mean Sq'] / nrow(paired))
stopifnot(abs(sqrt(vcov(reduced_fit)[2, 2]) - reduced_se) < 0.005,
          sqrt(vcov(specified_fit)[2, 2]) > reduced_se)
```

Where a reply does not state the residual mean square as R gives it, it rounds the value, as in 'about 41,000', or gives the residual variance, which is half of it. The paired interval appears only in replies to the open request, and the standard error of the specified model only in replies to the specified one.

The balance of the design made this arithmetic tractable. With every participant seeing every word after both types of prime, the restricted maximum likelihood (REML) fit of the model reduces to a few mean squares and cross-products of the paired differences and of their sums. From those quantities, every reply to the specified request reached the key features of the fit that lme4 reports, a by-participant slope with a standard deviation of about 9 ms whose correlation with the intercepts lay at the boundary (+1 in `r count_text(sum(positive_one))` replies and ±1 in the other).

### When the Design Is Unbalanced

In the unbalanced data, `r count_text(pairs_one_prime)` participant-word pairs are left with a trial after only one type of prime and `r count_text(pairs_no_trial, pairs_one_prime)` with no trial at all. Without balance, the estimate of the mixed model, `r ms(unbalanced_script$estimate)` ms in all `r count_text(runs_per_cell)` scripts, no longer equals the difference between the mean reaction times after the two types of prime, `r ms(unbalanced_raw_difference)` ms. Nor does the REML fit reduce to mean squares and cross-products, so it has to be found numerically. Removing the trials moved the lower bound of the Wald interval that the specified request fixed from `r ms(specified_script$lower)` to `r ms(unbalanced_script$lower)` ms, so that it no longer included zero. With Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, which the open-request scripts used, the same model gives `r interval(unbalanced_satterthwaite[1], unbalanced_satterthwaite[2])` ms, which still includes zero.

The prose replies approximated the model with weighted averages of the per-word effects and estimates of the variance components from the observed mean squares. Unlike the replies to the specified request on the balanced data, each of them put the variance of the by-participant slopes at or near zero. The fit that lme4 found kept a by-participant slope with a standard deviation of `r ms(attr(unbalanced_participant, 'stddev')[['prime_c']], 1)` ms, perfectly correlated with the intercepts. The replies' results therefore lie closer to those of the model without by-participant slopes, `r ms(reduced_numbers[1])` `r interval(reduced_numbers[2], reduced_numbers[3])` ms, than to the executed result. Table 3 sets the executed result beside those of the replies.

```{r}
# unbalanced_script (the executed result, which every script printed) and
# unbalanced_prose (the prose replies, in launch order) are built with the
# hidden checks earlier on the page.
knitr::kable(
  bind_rows(
    unbalanced_script |> transmute(Source = sprintf('Executed scripts (all %d)', runs_per_cell), result_text),
    unbalanced_prose |> transmute(Source = sprintf('Prose reply %d', row_number()), result_text)
  ) |> rename(`Estimate [95% interval] (ms)` = result_text),
  caption = paste('Results for the Unbalanced Data, as Each Run Wrote Them. The prose replies are numbered',
                  'in the order in which they were launched.'),
  align = c('l', 'r'))
```

At the precision each reply used, `r count_text(sum(unbalanced_signs[, 1] > 0))` of the `r count_text(nrow(unbalanced_prose))` estimates lay above the executed estimate, and the upper bounds fell on either side of the executed upper bound or matched it (Figure 1). Measured against the executed numbers to two decimals, the largest discrepancy in any of the three numbers was `r ms(max(largest_discrepancy), 2)` ms.

As the instructions allowed, every reply said that its numbers were approximations and gave a margin for them, from a few tenths of a millisecond to `r max(stated_margins$bounds)` ms, which in every case was wider than the discrepancy it covered. The errors in the lower bounds, however, all went one way. Every reply's lower bound lay above the executed one, as does that of the model without by-participant slopes. `r stringr::str_to_sentence(count_text(sum(near_zero)))` of the `r count_text(nrow(unbalanced_prose))` replies noted that the lower bound lay close to zero, and `r count_text(sum(depends_on_precision))` added that whether it excluded zero depended on the precision of their numbers. The executed lower bound lies only `r ms(unbalanced_script$lower, 2)` ms above zero, and the largest discrepancy in a lower bound amounts to `r sprintf('%.0f%%', 100 * max(unbalanced_prose$lower - unbalanced_script$lower) / unbalanced_script$lower)` of that distance, so only an executed model could show whether the exact interval excluded zero.

### Time Taken

Figure 2 shows how long each run took, from the request to the final reply. With the specified request, the scripts took a median of `r sprintf('%.1f', specified_script_minutes)` minutes, and the prose replies a median of `r sprintf('%.1f', minutes_of(condition_levels[2], 'prose'))` minutes on the balanced data and `r sprintf('%.1f', minutes_of(condition_levels[3], 'prose'))` on the unbalanced data. The difference is the work of computing by hand what each specified script computed in `r sprintf('%.1f', max(specified_seconds))` seconds or less when executed, R's start-up included. The open request took the scripts longer, with a median of `r count_text(open_tool_calls)` tool calls against `r count_text(specified_tool_calls)`, because the agents compared several random-effects structures and ran checks of their own. With that request, the scripts took from `r minutes_text(range_in('script', condition_levels[1])[1])` to `r minutes_text(range_in('script', condition_levels[1])[2])` minutes, overlapping the prose replies, which took from `r minutes_text(range_in('prose', condition_levels[1])[1])` to `r minutes_text(range_in('prose', condition_levels[1])[2])`. The runs shared one service and ran in batches, with `r count_text(main_still_running)` of the main runs still going when the follow-up was launched, so their durations include some waiting and are best read as orders of magnitude.

```{r minutes, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 3.6, fig.cap = cap_minutes, fig.alt = alt_minutes}
# In the specified conditions the two routes form separate clusters, which are
# labelled above those of the balanced data, at the geometric mean of each. A
# grey line marks the median of each route in each condition, which the text cites.
cluster_labels <- runs |>
  filter(condition == condition_levels[2]) |>
  group_by(route_label) |>
  summarise(minutes = exp(mean(log(minutes))), .groups = 'drop') |>
  mutate(label = ifelse(route_label == route_levels[1], 'Prose replies', 'Executed scripts'),
         condition = factor(condition_levels[2], levels = condition_levels))
medians <- runs |>
  group_by(condition, route_label) |>
  summarise(minutes = median(minutes), .groups = 'drop')

ggplot(runs, aes(minutes, condition, colour = route_label, shape = route_label)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(y = condition, xmin = minutes, xmax = minutes), data = medians, inherit.aes = FALSE,
                orientation = 'y', width = 0.42, linewidth = 0.7, colour = 'grey35') +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, fill = 'white', stroke = 0.9,
             position = position_jitter(width = 0, height = 0.12, seed = 1)) +
  geom_text(aes(minutes, condition, label = label), data = cluster_labels, inherit.aes = FALSE,
            nudge_y = 0.36, size = 3.4, colour = 'grey30') +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20), labels = c('0.5', '1', '2', '5', '10', '20')) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(condition_levels), labels = function(x) sub(', ', ',\n', x)) +
  route_scales +
  labs(x = 'Minutes (log scale)', y = NULL) +
  theme_depictr(base_size = 12, grid = 'x')
```

### Executing the Scripts Again

Executing a script again where it first ran tests whether it is deterministic, and executing it elsewhere tests whether its output depends on the environment. Every execution below ran in a fresh R process in the C locale, which fixes locale-dependent characters such as the quotation marks around the significance codes of a model summary. Outputs are compared line by line, so that Windows line endings do not count as a difference. Between them, the scripts load `r knitr::combine_words(packages_loaded, and = ' and ', oxford_comma = FALSE)`. Of these, lme4 relies on Matrix for its computations, and lmerTest calls pbkrtest for the Kenward–Roger degrees of freedom that `r count_text(kenward_scripts)` scripts compute.

```{r environment-record, include = FALSE}
scripts <- design |> filter(route == 'script')
n_scripts <- nrow(scripts)
stored <- executions |> filter(execution == 1)
stored_of <- function(run_id, column) stored[[column]][match(run_id, stored$run_id)]

# The versions an environment string records. packageVersion() writes a CRAN
# version such as 1.1-35.1 as 1.1.35.1, so the hyphen is restored.
cran <- function(version) sub('^([0-9]+\\.[0-9]+)\\.', '\\1-', version)
versions_of <- function(environment) {
  parts <- regmatches(environment, regexec(
    '^R ([^ ]+) \\(([^,]+), [^)]*\\) with lme4 ([^,]+), lmerTest ([^ ]+) and Matrix (.+)$',
    environment))[[1]]
  data.frame(System = if (grepl('linux', parts[3])) 'Linux' else if (grepl('mingw', parts[3])) 'Windows'
                      else if (grepl('darwin', parts[3])) 'macOS' else parts[3],
             R = parts[2], lme4 = cran(parts[4]), lmerTest = cran(parts[5]), Matrix = cran(parts[6]))
}
running_under <- function(file) {
  sub('^Running under: ', '', grep('^Running under:', readLines(file.path(experiment, file)),
                                   value = TRUE)[1])
}
stored_versions <- versions_of(unique(stored$environment))
stored_system <- running_under('executions_session_info.txt')
stored_release <- sub('^(Ubuntu [0-9]+\\.[0-9]+).*$', '\\1', stored_system)

# The stored environment rebuilt from its record by the Dockerfile, where
# verify_executions.R executed every script on GitHub Actions and listed the
# versions of the Ubuntu packages
verification <- read.csv(file.path(experiment, 'verification.csv'))
rebuild_record <- readLines(file.path(experiment, 'verification_session_info.txt'))
rebuild_release <- sub('^(Ubuntu [0-9]+\\.[0-9]+).*$', '\\1', running_under('verification_session_info.txt'))
rebuild_version <- function(package) {
  listed <- grep(sprintf('^r-cran-%s ', tolower(package)), rebuild_record, value = TRUE)
  sub('\\+.*$', '', sub('-[^-]+$', '', sub('^\\S+ ', '', listed)))
}

# The check on one machine with three package libraries that differ only in
# the versions of lme4 and lmerTest (check_versions.R), keeping the last
# attempt at each script
version_check <- read.csv(file.path(experiment, 'version_check.csv'))
checked <- version_check |>
  group_by(library, run_id) |> filter(attempt == max(attempt)) |> ungroup() |>
  mutate(same_output = status == 0 & stdout_sha256 == stored_of(run_id, 'stdout_sha256'),
         same_result = status == 0 & result == stored_of(run_id, 'result'))
library_rows <- function(library) checked[checked$library == library, ]
library_versions <- function(library) versions_of(unique(library_rows(library)$environment))
newer_versions <- library_versions('renv.lock')
newer_system <- sub('^(Windows [0-9]+).*$', '\\1', running_under('version_check_session_info.txt'))

# The versions of the other packages the scripts load, in the rebuild and in the
# library with the earlier lme4, and those that differ
library_version <- function(package, library) {
  listed <- unique(library_rows(library)$packages)
  sub(sprintf('^(.*, )?%s ([^,]+).*$', package), '\\2', listed)
}
other_packages <- c('emmeans', 'pbkrtest', 'dplyr', 'tidyr')
other_changed <- other_packages[vapply(other_packages, function(p)
  numeric_version(rebuild_version(p)) != numeric_version(library_version(p, 'lme4 1.1-35.1')),
  logical(1))]

# The two also differed in their linear-algebra libraries and in packages that
# lme4 depends on, such as nloptr, which the library with the earlier lme4 took
# from renv.lock
lock <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path('..', '..', '..', 'renv.lock'))
lapack_of <- function(file) grep('LAPACK', readLines(file.path(experiment, file)), value = TRUE)[1]
stopifnot(vapply(c('nloptr', 'minqa', 'Rcpp', 'RcppEigen'), function(p)
            numeric_version(rebuild_version(p)) != numeric_version(lock$Packages[[p]]$Version), logical(1)),
          lapack_of('verification_session_info.txt') != lapack_of('version_check_session_info.txt'))

# What the newer lme4 changed, from the kept outputs of the two libraries that
# differ only in its version. A printed table of random effects runs from its
# 'Groups' header to its 'Residual' row, and a likelihood-ratio table from its
# header to the next blank line.
read_output <- function(folder, id) {
  readLines(file.path(experiment, 'outputs', folder, paste0(id, '.txt')), warn = FALSE)
}
numbers_in <- function(lines) sort(unlist(regmatches(lines, gregexpr('-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?', lines))))
trailing_spaces <- function(lines) nchar(lines) - nchar(sub(' +$', '', lines))
changes <- bind_rows(lapply(scripts$run_id, function(id) {
  earlier <- read_output('stored-lme4', id)
  newer <- read_output('renv-lock', id)
  stopifnot(length(earlier) == length(newer))
  residual_rows <- grep('^ Residual ', newer)
  tables <- lapply(grep('^ Groups ', newer), function(start)
    start:min(residual_rows[residual_rows >= start]))
  correlated <- vapply(tables, function(rows) grepl('Corr', newer[rows[1]]), logical(1))
  renamed <- grep('-2*log(L)', newer, fixed = TRUE)
  renamed <- renamed[grepl('deviance', earlier[renamed])]
  blank <- which(trimws(newer) == '')
  ratio_tables <- unlist(lapply(renamed, function(start) start:(min(blank[blank > start]) - 1)))
  data.frame(
    run_id = id,
    correlated_tables = sum(correlated),
    one_more_space = all(vapply(tables[correlated], function(rows)
      all(trailing_spaces(newer[rows]) == trailing_spaces(earlier[rows]) + 1), logical(1))),
    uncorrelated_unchanged = all(vapply(tables[!correlated], function(rows)
      all(earlier[rows] == newer[rows]), logical(1))),
    reordered = sum(vapply(tables[correlated], function(rows)
      grepl('Std.Dev. Variance', earlier[rows[1]], fixed = TRUE) &&
        grepl('Variance +Std.Dev.', newer[rows[1]]), logical(1))),
    renamed = length(renamed),
    # every changed line lies in one of those tables
    explained = all(which(earlier != newer) %in% c(unlist(tables[correlated]), ratio_tables)),
    same_numbers = identical(numbers_in(earlier), numbers_in(sub('-2*log(L)', 'deviance', newer, fixed = TRUE))))
}))

# The claims of this section, of the discussion and of the summary and the
# abstract rest on these
libraries <- c('renv.lock', 'lme4 1.1-35.1', 'lme4 1.1-35.1 and lmerTest 3.1-3')
earlier_lme4 <- library_versions('lme4 1.1-35.1')
stopifnot(
  # the records are complete
  setequal(verification$run_id, scripts$run_id), setequal(unique(checked$library), libraries),
  all(table(checked$library)[libraries] == n_scripts),
  # each script ran once in the rebuild and in each library, as Table 4 says
  nrow(verification) == n_scripts, all(version_check$attempt == 1),
  # the rebuild matches the stored environment and reproduced its output
  unique(verification$environment) == unique(stored$environment), rebuild_release == stored_release,
  all(verification$identical),
  # the libraries differ only in lme4 and lmerTest, as the text says
```
